post_title: Ecoplastic Rural EB-5 Project | Hyundai Auto Parts Manufacturing Plant

acf.pro_desc_hero:
• A rural EB-5 project: Ecoplastic America's Phase 2 plant will manufacture interior and exterior plastic auto parts for Hyundai-Kia's U.S. assembly operations.
  • A Tier 1 supplier to Hyundai and Kia since 1984, with more than 40 years of direct supply to the automaker.
  • Located in a rural Targeted Employment Area (rural TEA), which qualifies Form I-526E petitions for priority processing by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).
  • Construction began in October 2025; operations are expected to start in Q4 2026.
  • Multiple layers of EB-5 loan repayment guarantees, including from Ecoplastic Corporation (KOSDAQ: 038110) and Seojin Automotive (KOSDAQ: 122690).

pro_parent_rp.pro_child_h3: Ecoplastic: an EB-5 project offered exclusively through IMM Group in Vietnam

pro_child_pr.pro_child_h5: Ecoplastic auto parts plant: project overview
pro_child_pr.pro_child_desc_n1:
• Manufactures interior and exterior auto parts such as bumpers, center consoles, body panels, and front trunks (frunks) for electric vehicles.
  • Technology: injection molding and robotic automated painting.
  • Supplies 3 Hyundai-Kia plants in the U.S.: Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America (HMGMA), Kia Georgia, and Hyundai Alabama.
  • Serves electric and hybrid models including the Hyundai IONIQ 5, IONIQ 9, and Palisade, and the Kia EV9 and Sportage.

• Not a project on paper: Phase 1 is complete and already in production in Georgia.
  • Phase 2 is being built next door, adding capacity in line with Hyundai and Kia's production growth plans.
  • The two plants share a common management system and operating chain.
  • Seamless supply to Hyundai-Kia assembly lines in the U.S.

• Hyundai's system sends a signal when a vehicle enters the assembly line.
  • Ecoplastic prepares parts matched to each vehicle's exact configuration within a 180-minute window (about 3 hours).
  • Parts are delivered directly to the assembly point at the Hyundai/Kia plant.
  • Synchronized with the supply chain to minimize inventory time and keep production on schedule.

• Total capitalization: US$112.7 million
  • EB-5 capital: US$79.2 million from 99 investors
  • Developer equity: US$33.5 million

pro_child_pr.pro_child_h5: Southeast Regional Center (SRC): specializing in rural EB-5 manufacturing projects
pro_child_pr.pro_child_desc_n1:
• More than 15 years of experience with rural EB-5 manufacturing projects.
  • Specializes in structuring EB-5 financing for auto parts plants in the Hyundai/Kia ecosystem in the U.S.
  • All of its previous projects have been approved by USCIS.
  • Investors in its projects have received green cards, and investors in matured projects have been repaid on the committed schedule.

pro_parent_rp.pro_child_h3: Strategic partner and Hyundai's market momentum

pro_child_pr.pro_child_h5: A Tier 1 Hyundai/Kia supplier for more than 40 years
pro_child_pr.pro_child_desc_n1:
• Working with Hyundai and Kia since 1984.
  • Supplies parts to Hyundai Metaplant (HMGMA) in Georgia, Kia Georgia, and Hyundai Alabama.
  • Market context: Hyundai's HMGMA megaplant targets production of 500,000 vehicles per year by 2028.

• Time from order to parts delivery: about 180 minutes
  • Meets Hyundai's JIT/JIS requirements
  • A competitive advantage over suppliers located farther from the assembly lines.

• 2025 sales: more than 1.19 million vehicles.
  • Hybrid sales up about 47%.
  • Strong sales for the IONIQ 5, Tucson, and Palisade.
  • Underpins demand for Ecoplastic's parts.

• 2026: approximately US$182.1 million (projected).
  • 2030: approximately US$808.1 million (projected).
  • Supplies multiple powertrains, including battery-electric, hybrid, and extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs), with new segments including the IONIQ 9, pickup trucks, and Genesis.

pro_child_pr.pro_child_h5: Rural TEA: priority processing by USCIS
pro_child_pr.pro_child_desc_n1:
• The project is located in a rural TEA as defined under the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 (RIA), enacted in March 2022.
  • Form I-526E petitions receive priority processing from USCIS under current rules.
  • Approval is anticipated in under 12 months, although actual processing times may vary.

• After Form I-526 approval, investors can draw on the 20% of EB-5 visas set aside for rural projects.
  • This may shorten the current wait for a visa.

pro_parent_rp.pro_child_h3: EB-5 job creation to support your green card

pro_child_pr.pro_child_desc_n1:
• Projected job creation: approximately 2,229 jobs (about 22.5 per EB-5 investor).
  • Jobs required for 99 investors: 990.
  • Job cushion: approximately 1,239 surplus jobs.

• Construction start: October 2025
  • Construction and pre-operational work are already laying the groundwork for EB-5 job creation.
  • As a Tier 1 Hyundai/Kia supplier, Ecoplastic has a strong incentive to complete the plant and begin operations on schedule.

pro_parent_rp.pro_child_h3: Structural features designed to manage EB-5 investment risk

pro_child_pr_item.pro_child_h4: 3 layers of repayment guarantees on the EB-5 loan

pro_child_pr.pro_child_desc_n1:
• A publicly listed Korean company and a Tier 1 Hyundai-Kia supplier for more than 40 years.
  • Provides a guarantee covering repayment of 100% of the EB-5 loan.
  • Committed to maintaining tangible net worth of at least US$200 million for the full term of the loan.
  • 2024 revenue: approximately US$1.69 billion.

pro_child_pr.pro_child_h5: Layer 2: the parent company that owns the U.S. project company
pro_child_pr.pro_child_desc_n1: • Provides a guarantee covering repayment of 100% of the EB-5 loan.

• A major shareholder of Ecoplastic Corporation (about 31.65% ownership).
  • Guarantees repayment of the EB-5 loan, liable for an amount equal to 31.65% of the total outstanding EB-5 loan balance.

• A first-position lien on the leasehold interest in the land and the Phase 2 plant buildings.
  • Takes effect once EB-5 disbursements reach US$20 million.

• A first-position lien on all machinery and equipment at the Phase 2 plant.
  •  Takes effect once EB-5 disbursements reach US$40 million.

• From 2030, the project must maintain a cash balance of more than US$40 million set aside for EB-5 loan repayment.
  • From 2031, this balance must exceed the total outstanding principal of the EB-5 loan.
  • No principal may be repaid to the parent company unless the reserve and liquidity conditions for the EB-5 loan have been met.

• Construction start: October 2025
  • Construction completion and start of operations: Q4 2026 (projected)
